title: Review and Compilation Engagements (SSARS)
exam_relevance: HIGHLY TESTED - Expect 4-6 questions on CPA AUD exam comparing reviews, compilations, and audits. Understanding the levels of assurance, required procedures, and report formats is essential. SSARS engagements are common for non-public companies.
learning_objectives: Understand the three levels of service: audit (high assurance), review (limited assurance), compilation (no assurance)
Master the required procedures for review engagements under SSARS
Understand compilation engagement requirements and when compilations are appropriate
Compare and contrast the assurance levels, procedures, and reports for each engagement type
Know the independence requirements for each engagement type
Understand proper report formats and wording for reviews and compilations
Identify when preparation services (no report) vs. compilation (with report) is appropriate
Apply the SSARS standards to determine appropriate engagement type for various client situations

introduction.overview: Statements on Standards for Accounting and Review Services (SSARS) provide guidance for CPAs who perform services on the financial statements of non-public companies. These services include preparation, compilation, and review engagements - all of which provide different levels of assurance than an audit.
introduction.why_important: Many non-public companies don't need or want the cost of a full audit. Reviews and compilations provide alternative services at lower cost with lower (or no) assurance.
introduction.key_standard: SSARS No. 21 (Clarification and Recodification of SSARS) as amended by subsequent standards, particularly SSARS No. 24 and 25, provides the primary guidance.
introduction.exam_context: The CPA exam heavily tests the differences between audit, review, and compilation - the procedures, assurance levels, and report formats. You must know how to distinguish them.

three_levels_of_service.description: CPAs can provide three primary levels of service related to financial statements, each with a different level of assurance.

audit.standards: Generally Accepted Auditing Standards (GAAS) - AU-C sections
audit.opinion_format: 'In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly...'
audit.procedures: Extensive substantive testing, control testing (if relying on controls), confirmation, observation, inspection
audit.typical_clients: Public companies (required), larger private companies, companies with debt covenants requiring audits

review.standards: SSARS (Statements on Standards for Accounting and Review Services)
review.conclusion_format: 'I am not aware of any material modifications that should be made...'
review.procedures: Primarily inquiry and analytical procedures - NO testing of assertions, NO confirmation, NO observation
review.cost_and_time: MODERATE cost and time (less than audit, more than compilation)
review.typical_clients: Mid-size private companies, companies that need some assurance but not a full audit, banks may accept reviews for smaller loans

compilation.assurance_level: NO assurance - just presenting management's statements
compilation.report_format: 'I did not audit or review... and accordingly, I do not express an opinion or provide any assurance...'
compilation.procedures: Minimal - read the FS, ensure they appear appropriate in form, ask questions if something appears incorrect
compilation.typical_clients: Small private companies, companies that need FS prepared but no assurance needed

preparation_service.description: SSARS also allows 'preparation' services where the accountant prepares FS but issues NO report
preparation_service.requirement: Each page of FS must include a statement: 'No assurance is provided on these financial statements'
preparation_service.when_used: When client only needs FS prepared and doesn't need a compilation report
preparation_service.independence_not_required: Accountant does not need to be independent for preparation services

three_levels_of_service.exam_focus: Know the hierarchy: Audit (high assurance) > Review (limited assurance) > Compilation (no assurance) > Preparation (no assurance, no report)

review_engagements.description: A review engagement provides LIMITED ASSURANCE that there are no material modifications that should be made to the financial statements for them to be in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

assurance_level.type: LIMITED (moderate) assurance - also called NEGATIVE assurance
assurance_level.meaning: The accountant's conclusion states they are NOT AWARE of any material modifications needed. This is weaker than an audit opinion that states FS 'present fairly.'
assurance_level.comparison_to_audit: Audit provides REASONABLE (high) assurance with positive opinion. Review provides LIMITED assurance with negative conclusion.
assurance_level.user_understanding: Users should understand that a review provides LESS assurance than an audit. There's a higher risk that a material misstatement could exist and not be detected in a review.

required_procedures.description: Review procedures are primarily INQUIRY and ANALYTICAL PROCEDURES. The accountant does NOT perform tests of details, confirmation, or observation.
inquiry_procedures: Inquire about accounting principles and practices
Inquire about procedures for recording, classifying, and summarizing transactions
Inquire about actions taken at meetings of stockholders, board of directors, and committees
Inquire whether FS are in accordance with applicable financial reporting framework
Inquire about significant transactions near period end
Inquire about status of uncorrected misstatements from prior periods
Inquire about unusual or complex situations that could affect FS
Inquire about significant journal entries and other adjustments
Inquire about communication from regulatory agencies
analytical_procedures: Compare current FS to prior periods and budgets
Compute and analyze financial ratios and trends
Compare key relationships (e.g., gross margin percentages)
Investigate significant unexpected differences or unusual relationships
Compare client's ratios to industry data
other_required_procedures: Obtain an understanding of the client's industry and knowledge of the client
Obtain understanding of accounting principles and practices of the industry
Read the financial statements to determine if they appear appropriate in form and free from obvious errors
Obtain a management representation letter (REQUIRED for reviews)

what_is_not_performed.no_confirmation: Do NOT send confirmations to customers, vendors, banks, or attorneys
what_is_not_performed.no_observation: Do NOT observe inventory counts or inspect assets
what_is_not_performed.no_tests_of_details: Do NOT examine invoices, contracts, or other supporting documents (unless something appears questionable)
what_is_not_performed.no_substantive_testing: Do NOT perform substantive tests of transactions or balances
what_is_not_performed.exam_emphasis: If a question asks what procedures are performed in a review and lists 'confirmation' or 'observation,' those are WRONG. Reviews = inquiry + analytical only.

independence_requirement.rule: The accountant MUST be independent to perform a review engagement
independence_requirement.reason: Because the review provides limited assurance, independence is essential to credibility
independence_requirement.if_not_independent: Cannot perform a review. Can only perform a compilation with disclosure of lack of independence in the report.
independence_requirement.exam_note: Independence is REQUIRED for reviews and audits. Independence is NOT required for compilations and preparations (but must disclose if not independent).

review_report_format.description: The review report has specific required elements and wording.
required_elements: Title that includes the word 'Independent' (if independent)
Introductory paragraph - states FS reviewed, engagement performed per SSARS, review primarily inquiry and analytical
Management's Responsibility - management responsible for preparation of FS
Accountant's Responsibility - describes review procedures and that review is less in scope than audit
Results/Conclusion paragraph - states whether accountant is aware of material modifications needed

key_conclusion_wording.unmodified_review_conclusion: 'Based on my review, I am not aware of any material modifications that should be made to the accompanying financial statements in order for them to be in accordance with [applicable financial reporting framework].'
key_conclusion_wording.negative_assurance: This is NEGATIVE assurance - states what the accountant is NOT aware of, rather than providing a positive opinion
key_conclusion_wording.exam_importance: Know this exact wording - exam often tests whether candidate recognizes proper review report language

departure_from_framework.situation: FS contain a material departure from GAAP (or applicable framework)
departure_from_framework.report_modification: Add a paragraph describing the departure and its effects. Conclusion is modified to state: 'With the exception of the matter described in the preceding paragraph, I am not aware of any material modifications...'

lack_of_independence.result: CANNOT perform a review. Must withdraw or downgrade to compilation with disclosure of lack of independence

scope_limitation.situation: Unable to perform all required review procedures
scope_limitation.result: Should withdraw from engagement OR modify report to describe scope limitation (not common in practice)

management_representation_letter.date: Dated as of the date of the review report
contents: Management is responsible for FS in accordance with applicable framework
Management believes FS are fairly presented
Management has provided all relevant information
Management has disclosed all material transactions and events
No subsequent events require adjustment or disclosure
Other matters relevant to the FS
management_representation_letter.exam_note: Representation letter is REQUIRED for reviews and audits. NOT required for compilations.

when_review_is_appropriate: Client needs some level of assurance but not a full audit
Cost of audit is prohibitive for client
Bank or other third party will accept a review (some lenders require audits, others accept reviews for smaller loans)
Owners want more than compilation but less than audit
Mid-size private companies commonly use reviews

compilation_engagements.description: A compilation engagement involves assisting management in presenting financial information in the form of financial statements WITHOUT providing any assurance on those statements.

assurance_level.meaning: The accountant simply helps prepare/present the FS in proper format. The accountant does NOT express an opinion or conclusion. Users get NO assurance from the accountant.
assurance_level.user_understanding: The compilation report explicitly states the accountant provides NO assurance. Users understand they are relying solely on management, not on any verification by the accountant.

required_procedures.description: Compilation procedures are MINIMAL - much less than a review or audit.
what_is_required: Obtain understanding of the client's industry and operations
Obtain understanding of accounting principles and practices in the client's industry
Obtain knowledge of the client sufficient to compile FS
READ the financial statements to ensure they appear appropriate in form and are free from obvious material errors
If something appears incorrect or incomplete, inquire with management (but not required to verify)
what_is_not_required: NO inquiry procedures (beyond addressing obvious errors)
NO management representation letter (not required for compilations)
NO verification of information provided by management
required_procedures.essence: The accountant essentially takes management's information, puts it into proper financial statement format, reads it for obvious errors, and issues a report saying 'I didn't provide any assurance.'
required_procedures.exam_emphasis: Compilations require almost NO procedures. Just read the FS for obvious errors and ensure proper form. If question asks about procedures in a compilation, the answer is usually 'minimal' or 'none.'

independence_not_required.rule: The accountant does NOT need to be independent to perform a compilation
independence_not_required.disclosure_if_not_independent: If the accountant is NOT independent, must disclose the lack of independence in the compilation report
independence_not_required.disclosure_wording: Add a final paragraph: 'I am not independent with respect to XYZ Company.'
independence_not_required.no_reason_needed: The report should NOT describe the reasons for lack of independence (just state the fact)
independence_not_required.exam_distinction: Independence is REQUIRED for review and audit. Independence is NOT required for compilation and preparation (but must disclose if not independent).

compilation_report_format.description: The compilation report explicitly states NO assurance is provided.
required_elements: Title (does NOT need to include 'Independent' if not independent)
Introductory paragraph - states FS were compiled
Management's Responsibility - management responsible for FS
Accountant's Responsibility - states compilation performed per SSARS, accountant did not audit or review, does not express opinion or provide assurance

key_wording.no_assurance_statement: 'I did not audit or review the accompanying financial statements and, accordingly, I do not express an opinion, a conclusion, nor provide any assurance on them.'
key_wording.exam_importance: This exact language is heavily tested. The report explicitly says NO opinion, NO conclusion, NO assurance.

departure_from_framework.situation: FS contain a known departure from GAAP
accountant_options: Option 1: Do not include the departure in report (just compile as presented by management - assuming departure is adequately disclosed)
Option 2: Add a paragraph describing the departure (if accountant believes it's important to highlight)
departure_from_framework.key_point: Because NO assurance is provided, the accountant is not required to modify the report for GAAP departures. However, if the FS omit substantially all disclosures, this must be disclosed in the report.

substantially_all_disclosures_omitted.situation: FS omit substantially all note disclosures (common for compiled statements)
substantially_all_disclosures_omitted.requirement: MUST add a paragraph disclosing the omission
substantially_all_disclosures_omitted.wording: 'Management has elected to omit substantially all of the disclosures ordinarily included in financial statements prepared in accordance with [framework]. If the omitted disclosures were included in the financial statements, they might influence the user's conclusions about the company's financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.'
substantially_all_disclosures_omitted.exam_note: This is VERY common in compilations - many small businesses want FS without notes. Must disclose the omission in the compilation report.

lack_of_independence.requirement: Add final paragraph: 'I am not independent with respect to XYZ Company.'
lack_of_independence.no_reason_given: Do NOT explain why not independent

when_compilation_is_appropriate: Small businesses that need FS for tax return or internal use
No third-party users requiring assurance (no bank loan, no investors)
Client cannot afford review or audit
Management just needs help putting books into financial statement format
FS are for management use only
Very common for small private companies

preparation_engagements.description: Preparation services involve preparing FS without issuing a report. This is the lowest level of service under SSARS.
preparation_engagements.no_report_issued: The key distinction from compilation is that NO report is issued. The accountant just prepares the FS.

requirements.legend_on_each_page: Each page of the FS must include a legend: 'No assurance is provided on these financial statements.'
requirements.procedures: Same minimal procedures as compilation - obtain understanding, read FS for obvious errors
requirements.independence_not_required: Accountant does not need to be independent (no report issued, so no disclosure needed)
requirements.documentation: Must document understanding with client that no report will be issued

when_used: Client only needs FS prepared, doesn't need a formal compilation report
Cost savings - slightly less expensive than compilation because no report prepared
FS are for internal use or tax preparation only
preparation_engagements.exam_note: Preparation services are newer to SSARS (added in recent years) and less frequently tested than compilation and review. Know the basic concept: NO report, just legend on each page.

comparison_table.description: Side-by-side comparison of the four service levels - CRITICAL for exam

procedures.audit: Extensive - tests of details, confirmation, observation, analytical procedures, inquiry, control testing (if relying), inspection
procedures.review: INQUIRY and ANALYTICAL procedures primarily. Read FS. No confirmation, observation, or testing.
procedures.compilation: MINIMAL - obtain understanding, READ FS for obvious errors, inquire if something appears wrong

independence_required.compilation: NO - not required (but must disclose if not independent)
independence_required.preparation: NO - not required (no disclosure since no report)

report_issued.compilation: YES - compilation report stating no assurance
report_issued.preparation: NO - no report (just legend on FS)

report_key_language.audit: 'In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly...'
report_key_language.review: 'I am not aware of any material modifications that should be made...'
report_key_language.compilation: 'I did not audit or review... and do not express an opinion, conclusion, or provide any assurance...'

standards.audit: GAAS (Generally Accepted Auditing Standards - AU-C sections)
standards.review: SSARS (Statements on Standards for Accounting and Review Services)

decision_framework.description: How to determine which engagement type is appropriate

q1_regulatory_requirement.question: Is an audit REQUIRED by regulation, loan covenant, or other agreement?

q2_assurance_needed.question: Do users need assurance on the financial statements?

q3_level_of_assurance.question: Do users need HIGH assurance or would LIMITED assurance suffice?
q3_level_of_assurance.limited_sufficient: Perform REVIEW (if users will accept limited assurance and cost is a factor)

q4_report_needed.question: Is a formal report needed, or is the client just requesting FS preparation?

common_scenarios.scenario_2: Large private company with bank loan → Usually AUDIT (required by lender)
common_scenarios.scenario_3: Mid-size private company, bank will accept review → REVIEW
common_scenarios.scenario_4: Small business, no external users → COMPILATION or PREPARATION
common_scenarios.scenario_5: Company just needs help with bookkeeping and FS for taxes → PREPARATION

omitted_disclosures.description: Compiled FS frequently omit substantially all note disclosures (saves cost)
omitted_disclosures.requirement: Must disclose the omission in the compilation report
omitted_disclosures.not_gaap: FS without notes are NOT in accordance with GAAP, but this is acceptable for compilations as long as disclosed
omitted_disclosures.exam_note: Very common exam question - compiled statements omit notes, what should the report say? Answer: add paragraph disclosing omission.

change_in_engagement_level.description: Client may request change from audit to review, or review to compilation
reasons_for_request: Change in circumstances (no longer need high assurance)
accountant_considerations: Consider whether request is reasonable or if client is trying to avoid adverse findings
If scope limitation caused the request, may not be able to issue review or compilation report either (if limitation affects ability to form any conclusion)
Must consider whether already-performed procedures would cause issues (e.g., if auditor already found material misstatement, can't ignore it in review or compilation)
change_in_engagement_level.exam_scenario: Client requests change from audit to review after auditor finds going concern issue. Should auditor accept? Answer: Depends on reason - if trying to avoid going concern disclosure, likely should not accept.

reporting_on_comparative_statements.description: When FS include comparative prior year, accountant must address the prior year
reporting_on_comparative_statements.same_level_both_years: If review or compilation for both years, issue single report covering both years
reporting_on_comparative_statements.different_levels: If current year review but prior year compilation, must state the difference in service level in the report and describe the lower assurance for prior year

practice_problems.question:
Match each procedure to the engagement type(s) where it IS performed:

Procedures:
A. Send confirmations to accounts receivable customers
B. Perform inquiry and analytical procedures
C. Obtain management representation letter
D. Read financial statements for obvious errors
E. Observe physical inventory count
F. Test internal controls
G. Examine vendor invoices and other supporting documents

Engagement Types:
1. Audit
2. Review
3. Compilation
4. Preparation

solution.A_confirmations: 1 (Audit only) - Confirmations are NOT performed in reviews, compilations, or preparations
solution.B_inquiry_analytical: 1 (Audit) and 2 (Review) - Both audits and reviews use inquiry and analytical procedures. Reviews use them as primary procedures. NOT performed in compilations or preparations.
solution.C_management_rep_letter: 1 (Audit) and 2 (Review) - Representation letters are REQUIRED for audits and reviews. NOT required for compilations or preparations.
solution.D_read_FS: 1 (Audit), 2 (Review), 3 (Compilation), and 4 (Preparation) - Reading the FS is performed in ALL engagement types. It's a basic procedure in all services.
solution.E_inventory_observation: 1 (Audit only) - Observation is an audit procedure. NOT performed in reviews, compilations, or preparations.
solution.F_test_controls: 1 (Audit only - if relying on controls) - Control testing is an audit procedure. NOT performed in reviews, compilations, or preparations.
solution.G_examine_documents: 1 (Audit primarily) - Examining supporting documents is primarily an audit procedure (tests of details). NOT routinely performed in reviews (unless something appears questionable). NOT performed in compilations or preparations (unless obvious error noticed).
key_takeaways: Inquiry and analytical - AUDIT and REVIEW (but primary in review)
Management representation letter - AUDIT and REVIEW only
Compilation and preparation have MINIMAL procedures

practice_problems.question:
For each scenario, determine the appropriate engagement type and explain your reasoning:

Scenario A: ABC Company is a small family-owned business with annual revenue of $500,000. The owners need financial statements for their tax return and for their own records. No bank loans or external investors. The owners have asked the CPA to prepare the financial statements.

Scenario B: DEF Company is a mid-size manufacturing company with revenue of $10 million. The company has a bank loan, and the bank has stated they will accept either an audit or a review. Management wants to save costs but needs the bank to be satisfied.

Scenario C: GHI Company is a public company traded on NYSE.

Scenario D: JKL Company is a small business that needs financial statements compiled for a potential investor. The CPA who will perform the service owns 10% of the company and is not independent.

scenario_A.recommended_engagement: PREPARATION service (or compilation if formal report desired)

reasoning.assurance_needed: NO - no external users requiring assurance (just for taxes and internal use)
reasoning.independence_consideration: Independence not required for preparation or compilation
reasoning.cost: Preparation is lowest cost, which seems appropriate for small business with no assurance needs
reasoning.alternative: Compilation could work if owners want a formal report, but preparation saves cost and is sufficient for stated needs

scenario_A.report: If preparation service: NO report issued, just legend on each page 'No assurance is provided.' If compilation: compilation report stating no assurance provided.

reasoning.bank_will_accept_review: Bank stated they will accept review or audit - review provides sufficient assurance at lower cost
reasoning.cost_savings: Review is significantly less expensive than audit and appropriate when limited assurance is acceptable
reasoning.independence_required: CPA must be independent to perform review

scenario_B.report: Review report with conclusion: 'Based on my review, I am not aware of any material modifications that should be made...'
scenario_B.procedures: Inquiry and analytical procedures, management representation letter, read financial statements

reasoning.regulatory_requirement: Public companies are REQUIRED by SEC to have audits
reasoning.no_option: No choice - must be an audit
reasoning.standards: Audit must comply with PCAOB standards (for public companies) and SEC requirements

scenario_C.report: Audit report with opinion: 'In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly...'

scenario_D.recommended_engagement: COMPILATION with disclosure of lack of independence

reasoning.not_independent: CPA owns 10% of company - NOT independent
reasoning.independence_required_for_review: Cannot perform review or audit (independence required)
reasoning.can_perform_compilation: CAN perform compilation even if not independent - must disclose lack of independence
reasoning.assurance_provided: NO assurance provided - investor understands this from compilation report

scenario_D.report_modification: Standard compilation report PLUS additional final paragraph: 'I am not independent with respect to JKL Company.' Do NOT explain the reason for lack of independence (ownership).
scenario_D.cannot_do: CANNOT perform a review (independence required). If client needs assurance, must engage a different CPA who is independent.

key_exam_concepts: No assurance needed, no external users = preparation or compilation
Limited assurance acceptable and cost is factor = review
Public company or regulatory requirement = audit
Not independent = can compile (with disclosure) but cannot review or audit

practice_problems.question:
A CPA is engaged to perform a compilation of financial statements for MNO Company. During the engagement, the following issues arise:

Issue 1: The financial statements omit substantially all note disclosures. Management states they want to save costs and notes are not needed for their purposes.

Issue 2: While reading the financial statements, the CPA notices that depreciation expense seems unusually low compared to the company's fixed assets. The amount is material.

Issue 3: Management informs the CPA that they use the cash basis of accounting, not the accrual basis.

Required:
1. How should the CPA address each issue in the compilation engagement?
2. What modifications (if any) are required to the compilation report for each issue?
3. Can the CPA complete the compilation engagement, or must the CPA withdraw?

issue_1_omitted_disclosures.how_to_address: This is ACCEPTABLE for a compilation. Compiled financial statements frequently omit substantially all disclosures to save costs. The CPA should understand management's reason and ensure they understand the implications.
issue_1_omitted_disclosures.report_modification_REQUIRED: YES - MUST add a paragraph to the compilation report disclosing the omission of substantially all disclosures.
issue_1_omitted_disclosures.paragraph_wording: 'Management has elected to omit substantially all of the disclosures ordinarily included in financial statements prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. If the omitted disclosures were included in the financial statements, they might influence the user's conclusions about the Company's financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.'
issue_1_omitted_disclosures.can_complete_engagement: YES - this is common and acceptable in compilations
issue_1_omitted_disclosures.exam_note: Omitted disclosures in compilations is VERY commonly tested. Remember: acceptable but MUST disclose in report.

issue_2_unusual_depreciation.how_to_address: The CPA noticed something that appears incorrect or incomplete. In a compilation, the CPA should INQUIRE with management about the unusual item. The CPA is not required to verify management's response, but should ask the question.
issue_2_unusual_depreciation.inquiry: Ask management: 'Depreciation expense appears low relative to fixed assets. Can you explain this?'
possible_management_responses: Management explains: 'We have new accounting software that calculated it differently' - CPA should consider if explanation makes sense
Management explains: 'We accelerated depreciation in prior years' - CPA should consider if explanation is reasonable
Management cannot explain or explanation doesn't make sense - CPA should request correction or explanation
issue_2_unusual_depreciation.report_modification: If management provides reasonable explanation, NO modification needed to compilation report (CPA is not verifying, just compiling). If management cannot explain or refuses to investigate, CPA should consider whether FS are appropriate for compilation or whether withdrawal is necessary.
issue_2_unusual_depreciation.key_point: In compilations, CPA inquires if something appears obviously wrong but does NOT verify. If management's explanation is reasonable, proceed. If management refuses to address obvious error, may need to withdraw.
issue_2_unusual_depreciation.exam_principle: Compilation procedures are MINIMAL, but if CPA sees obvious material error, must inquire. Not required to verify management's response.

issue_3_cash_basis.how_to_address: Management is using cash basis instead of accrual basis GAAP. This is a departure from GAAP.
issue_3_cash_basis.compilation_allows_departures: In a compilation, the CPA can compile financial statements that depart from GAAP (because no assurance is provided). The CPA does NOT have to modify the compilation report for GAAP departures UNLESS they want to highlight it.
report_modification_options: Option 1: Do NOT modify the report - just compile the cash basis statements as presented. The compilation report already states the CPA provides NO assurance.
Option 2: ADD a paragraph describing the departure from GAAP if the CPA believes it's important to highlight for users.
issue_3_cash_basis.most_common_approach: For compilation, usually do NOT modify the report for GAAP departures. The report already says no assurance is provided. However, the CPA should ensure that the financial statements DISCLOSE the basis of accounting used (e.g., note saying 'These FS are prepared on the cash basis').
issue_3_cash_basis.can_complete_engagement: YES - can compile cash basis statements. No assurance is provided, so GAAP departure is acceptable.
issue_3_cash_basis.exam_note: Compilations can include GAAP departures without report modification (because no assurance provided). However, substantially all disclosures omitted MUST be disclosed in report.

summary_answers.can_complete_engagement: YES - all three issues are addressable and the CPA can complete the compilation
summary_answers.required_modifications: ONLY Issue 1 (omitted disclosures) REQUIRES a report modification. Issues 2 and 3 do NOT require modifications (though CPA should inquire about issue 2).
summary_answers.procedures: Issue 1: disclose in report. Issue 2: inquire with management. Issue 3: acceptable, no action required (assuming basis is disclosed in FS).

solution.key_exam_takeaway: Compilations provide NO assurance and can include GAAP departures. HOWEVER, if substantially all disclosures are omitted, MUST disclose that in the compilation report. If CPA notices something obviously wrong while reading FS, should inquire, but not required to verify.

tip_1_know_the_hierarchy.description: Memorize the assurance hierarchy and how it affects procedures and reports
tip_1_know_the_hierarchy.hierarchy: Audit (high assurance) > Review (limited assurance) > Compilation (no assurance) > Preparation (no assurance, no report)
tip_1_know_the_hierarchy.exam_strategy: When question asks about procedures, think about assurance level. High assurance = extensive procedures. No assurance = minimal procedures.

tip_2_procedures_by_engagement.description: Know which procedures are performed in which engagements
tip_2_procedures_by_engagement.audit_only: Confirmation, observation, inspection of assets, tests of details, control testing
tip_2_procedures_by_engagement.audit_and_review: Inquiry, analytical procedures, reading FS, management representation letter
tip_2_procedures_by_engagement.all_engagements: Reading FS for obvious errors, obtaining understanding of client/industry
tip_2_procedures_by_engagement.exam_trap: If question asks about review procedures and includes 'confirmation' as an option - WRONG. Reviews do NOT confirm.

tip_3_independence_requirements.required: Audit and Review - MUST be independent
tip_3_independence_requirements.not_required: Compilation and Preparation - independence NOT required (but must disclose if not independent for compilation)
tip_3_independence_requirements.disclosure: If not independent and performing compilation, add paragraph: 'I am not independent with respect to [Company].' Do NOT explain why.
tip_3_independence_requirements.exam_scenario: Question says CPA owns stock in client. Ask which service can be performed? Answer: Compilation with disclosure, or Preparation. Cannot do review or audit.

tip_4_management_representation_letter.description: Know when management representation letter is required
tip_4_management_representation_letter.exam_question: Question asks which procedure is performed in a review. If 'obtain management representation letter' is an option, it's CORRECT.

tip_5_report_language.description: Memorize the key language for each report type - heavily tested
tip_5_report_language.audit: 'In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects...'
tip_5_report_language.review: 'Based on my review, I am not aware of any material modifications that should be made...'
tip_5_report_language.compilation: 'I did not audit or review the financial statements and, accordingly, I do not express an opinion, a conclusion, nor provide any assurance on them.'
tip_5_report_language.exam_question: Question shows report excerpt and asks what type of engagement. Look for key phrases.

tip_6_omitted_disclosures.description: Omitted disclosures in compilations is very commonly tested
tip_6_omitted_disclosures.rule: Compiled FS can omit substantially all disclosures, but MUST disclose the omission in the compilation report
tip_6_omitted_disclosures.required_paragraph: Add paragraph stating management elected to omit disclosures and that they might influence users' conclusions
tip_6_omitted_disclosures.exam_scenario: Question describes compiled statements without notes. What should report say? Answer: add paragraph about omitted disclosures.

tip_7_gaap_departures.description: Know how GAAP departures are handled differently by engagement type
tip_7_gaap_departures.audit: Material departure = qualified or adverse opinion (depending on pervasiveness)
tip_7_gaap_departures.review: Material departure = modified conclusion ('With the exception of the matter described...')
tip_7_gaap_departures.compilation: Departure is ACCEPTABLE - no report modification required (but CAN add paragraph if want to highlight). Exception: must disclose if substantially all disclosures omitted.
tip_7_gaap_departures.exam_distinction: Audits and reviews must modify for GAAP departures. Compilations do NOT have to (because no assurance).

tip_8_review_uses_inquiry_and_analytical.description: Reviews use PRIMARILY inquiry and analytical procedures - no confirmation, observation, or testing
tip_8_review_uses_inquiry_and_analytical.memorize: Review = Inquiry + Analytical (that's it - nothing else except reading FS and management rep letter)
tip_8_review_uses_inquiry_and_analytical.exam_trap: If question about review includes 'send confirmations' or 'observe inventory' - WRONG
tip_8_review_uses_inquiry_and_analytical.why_limited: Limited assurance requires less procedures than high assurance. Inquiry and analytical provide enough basis for negative assurance.

tip_9_preparation_vs_compilation.description: Know the difference between preparation and compilation
tip_9_preparation_vs_compilation.preparation: NO report issued. Just legend on each page of FS: 'No assurance is provided.'
tip_9_preparation_vs_compilation.compilation: Report IS issued stating no assurance provided
tip_9_preparation_vs_compilation.when_to_use_each: If client just needs FS prepared with no formal report = preparation. If client wants formal report = compilation.
tip_9_preparation_vs_compilation.exam_note: Preparation is newer to SSARS and less frequently tested, but know the basic difference (report vs. no report).

tip_10_comparative_statements.description: When reporting on multiple years with different service levels
tip_10_comparative_statements.rule: If current year review but prior year compilation, must state in report that prior year was compilation with lower assurance
tip_10_comparative_statements.reason: Users need to understand that different levels of assurance apply to different years
tip_10_comparative_statements.exam_scenario: Question asks about reporting on comparative statements with different service levels. Answer: disclose the difference and describe lower assurance for prior year.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Which procedure is performed in a review engagement?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Look for inquiry, analytical procedures, or management representation letter. Eliminate confirmation, observation, tests of details.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: CPA is not independent. Which service can be performed?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Compilation (with disclosure) or Preparation. Cannot do Review or Audit.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Compiled statements omit all disclosures. What should report say?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Must add paragraph disclosing that substantially all disclosures are omitted.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Show excerpt of report and ask what type of engagement
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Look for key phrases: 'present fairly' = audit, 'not aware of modifications' = review, 'do not express opinion or provide assurance' = compilation

Use hierarchy - audit has most procedures, preparation has least. Independence required for audit/review, not for compilation/preparation. Rep letter for audit/review, not for compilation/preparation.

memorization_aids.independence_mnemonic: I R Independent (Audit and Review require Independence)
memorization_aids.rep_letter_mnemonic: Reps for A and R (Representation letter for Audit and Review)
memorization_aids.review_procedures: I + A = Review (Inquiry + Analytical = Review procedures)
memorization_aids.compilation_no_assurance: Compilation = No Opinion, No Conclusion, No Assurance (remember the three NOs)

key_concepts: Four service levels: Audit (high assurance), Review (limited assurance), Compilation (no assurance with report), Preparation (no assurance, no report)
Audit uses extensive procedures including confirmation, observation, testing. Review uses primarily inquiry and analytical. Compilation uses minimal procedures (read FS).
Independence REQUIRED for audit and review. NOT required for compilation and preparation (must disclose if not independent for compilation).
Management representation letter REQUIRED for audit and review. NOT required for compilation and preparation.
Review report provides NEGATIVE assurance: 'I am not aware of any material modifications...'
Compilation report explicitly states NO assurance: 'I do not express an opinion, conclusion, or provide any assurance'
Compiled FS can omit substantially all disclosures, but MUST disclose the omission in the compilation report
GAAP departures must be addressed in audit and review reports, but NOT required to modify compilation report (no assurance provided)
Preparation service issues NO report, just legend on FS pages
critical_for_exam: Know procedures by engagement type: Audit (extensive) > Review (inquiry + analytical) > Compilation (minimal)
Know assurance levels: High (audit) > Limited (review) > None (compilation/preparation)
Independence required for audit/review, not for compilation/preparation
Rep letter required for audit/review, not for compilation/preparation
Memorize key report language for each engagement type
Omitted disclosures in compilation MUST be disclosed in report
Reviews use inquiry + analytical ONLY - no confirmation, observation, or testing
common_mistakes: Thinking reviews include confirmations or observation - they don't, only inquiry and analytical
Thinking independence is required for compilations - it's not (but must disclose if not independent)
Thinking compiled statements cannot have GAAP departures - they can (no assurance provided)
Forgetting to disclose omitted disclosures in compilation report - this IS required
Confusing negative assurance (review) with no assurance (compilation)
Thinking compilation provides some assurance - it provides NONE
